Thanks for the ping, Chloe — reviewed the redlines. Legal comments / suggested positions: 

1) Credit cap: we should propose a cap expressed as a percentage of the monthly recurring charges (MRC). Suggested starting point: 25% cap per month, 50% cap cumulative over a 12-month rolling period. Absolute uncapped credits are not acceptable.

2) Uptime definition and measurement: insist on single-source measurement (Redwood monitoring endpoint) with regional carveouts. If ACME requires 99.99, tie that to multi-region active-active deployment and a documented failover plan. Otherwise propose 99.95 for single-region.

3) Scheduled maintenance: legal OK with a weekly short maintenance window (e.g., up to 2 hours/week) with notification at least 72 hours in advance. For larger maintenance (>30 minutes impact), require 2 weeks' notice and allow customers to opt-out for a single-week blackout per quarter.

4) Response times: P1 / P2 definitions should be objective (e.g., P1 = production outage preventing requests; P2 = degraded performance). P1 within 1 hour is our standard ask; 30-minute P1 can be provided as a commercial concession for a higher tier or Dedicated commit.

I've attached a marked-up set of redlines (SLA_line_item_diff.docx) with exact language edits. If sales wants to offer anything closer to ACME's ask, we should get explicit approval from Revenue Ops for a credits cap exception.

—Marissa

Operational notes from an SRE lens: 

- 99.99% monthly availability (≈4.3 minutes/month downtime) is achievable only with multi-region active-active and guaranteed failover. For single-region deployments we should not commit to 99.99. Recommend offering 99.95 (≈21.6 minutes/month) for single-region customers and 99.99 for multi-region with documented runbooks and a DR SLA.

- P1 within 30 minutes is aggressive given on-call routing and incident validation. We typically commit to P1 response acknowledgement within 60 minutes, resolution SLA dependent on severity. If Acme requires 30 minutes, we should require a Dedicated or higher-priority support add-on.

- Credits model: per-incident minute-level credits are operationally complex; prefer tiered credit bands (e.g., <99.95 = 10%, 99.90–99.95 = 15%, <99.90 = 25%) with monthly cap.

- Maintenance: we run rolling updates and can avoid customer-impacting maintenance during customer business hours most weeks, but some security patches require immediate attention. Propose: weekly patch window: Sun 02:00–04:00 UTC by default; customers can request a blackout for one such window per quarter. Major upgrades: 2-week notice.

I'll attach a short ops note and a suggested SLA matrix (SLA_comparison.xlsx).

—Rishi

Tom — thanks for the redlines and context. Internal feedback below and a proposed middle-ground to unblock the order form so your procurement team can move to signature.

Proposed Redwood position (compromise):
- Uptime: 99.95% monthly for single-region deployments (this is our standard). 99.99% can be provided for multi-region active-active with an explicit runbook and a deployment addendum.
- Service credits: tiered bands with a monthly cap at 25% of MRC. Suggested bands: <99.95 = 10% credit; <99.90 = 25% credit. We cannot accept an uncapped credits model.
- Response times: P1 acknowledgement within 1 hour; P2 acknowledgement within 4 hours. For customers that require 30-minute P1 acknowledgement we can offer a Priority Support add-on (Dedicated or Premier).
- Maintenance windows: default weekly patch slot Sun 02:00–04:00 UTC; 72 hours' notice for routine maintenance, 2 weeks' notice for major upgrades (>30 min impact). Customers can request one blackout per quarter for a weekly patch window. Emergency security patches are excluded from blackout restrictions but will be communicated as early as possible.

Attachments: marked redlines and an SLA matrix that maps availability to credits and typical runbooks. If this is acceptable to ACME we can update the Order Form and circulate a DocuSign envelope. If you prefer to push for 99.99 in the MSA, please indicate whether Acme is willing to commit to multi-region deployment + the additional monthly fee for the higher SLA.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call with your procurement and engineering leads to close this out — how does Monday 9/14 10:00 PT look?
